tasks.short: Guide and counsel students on academic adjustment

steps.what: Guide and counsel students on adjustments, academic problems and special academic interests

tasks.design: Keep guidance and counselling with the teacher. Existing support information in the {OTHER} pupil record system can inform the conversation, but no new record preparation or automated counselling step is assumed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Useful guidance depends on trust, the student's perspective and context.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing information tools support the teacher without replacing the relationship.
tasks.still_hard: Understanding the underlying concern and recognising when specialist help is needed.
tasks.human_edge: Listening, reassurance and helping the student make choices.
tasks.altitude: No change to counselling time or professional boundaries.

reach.task: Refer a concern needing specialist assessment

evidence.claim: Keeping student counselling human is an E1 judgement; the digest's preparation tools do not establish counselling savings.

assumptions: Boundary is direct guidance and counselling, excluding separate lesson preparation and formal support plans.
The teacher elicits concerns during the fully retained interaction. No structured concern code, inferred emotion or automated diagnosis is assumed.
Zero upkeep because no new workflow or software is introduced.
unknowns: Student concerns and local referral arrangements
research_questions: Which academic concerns require support beyond the teacher's remit?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Direct guidance remains fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Monitor adherence to inclusive education requirements

steps.what: Gather applicable special education program requirements and existing delivery records
Monitor teachers and teacher assistants through direct observation and discussion
Discuss adherence concerns and agree corrective teaching actions

tasks.design: Configure saved access-limited views of applicable requirements in {DOCS} and existing records in the {OTHER} pupil record system. Keep direct observation, interpretation and corrective discussions with the authorised teacher; no automatic staff-compliance score is produced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Relevant requirements and existing delivery evidence require repeated retrieval.
tasks.enabler_now: Native folders and filtered views can collect source material without judging staff performance.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguishing a justified adaptation from a failure to provide agreed support.
tasks.human_edge: Contextual observation and constructive professional feedback.
tasks.altitude: Less document retrieval; oversight rights are unchanged.

reach.task: Clarify an inclusive programme requirement before discussing delivery

evidence.claim: Saved requirement views are an E1 proposal; the digest does not demonstrate automated monitoring of inclusive teaching adherence.

assumptions: Boundary is the focal teacher's preparation, observation and feedback, excluding other staff work and formal HR decisions.

Authorised support planning produces the existing programme requirements and delivery staff produce normal records. In s1 the focal teacher checks pupil or group reference, programme version, requirement applicability and access; capture and manual retrieval stay in its 12 retained hours.
No new checklist completion, structured adherence flag or recording is requested from colleagues. Missing records require direct clarification in retained s2.
Test native views first. Local oversight authority and national school consultation requirements must be confirmed; no cameras or staff ranking are introduced.
unknowns: Existing record completeness and retrieval burden
research_questions: Can preparation views reduce retrieval without turning missing documentation into an assumed compliance failure?

incremental.description: Maintain requirement links, filters and access

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=20*0.60+50+30=92; gross=8, upkeep=2, net=6. High assumes repeated retrieval; low assumes existing effective views give no gross saving while upkeep remains.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan and conduct balanced instructional activities

steps.what: Choose learning goals and capture participation, access and timing constraints
Plan a balanced sequence of instruction, demonstration, investigation and work time

loop.purpose: Draft a sequence from supplied teaching resources and teacher constraints
loop.input: Activity brief and approved source activities
loop.output: Draft sequence with goal links, participation options and timings
loop.check: Teacher checks learning demand, activity suitability, access and whether timings leave real questioning and investigation opportunities
loop.stop: One draft and one revision, then manual planning
loop.why_not_simpler: Selecting and describing a coherent sequence from varied activity text requires semantic reading; timing arithmetic stays deterministic

steps.what: Check and approve the exact activity sequence before teaching
Conduct activities and adapt instruction, demonstrations and work time to student responses

tasks.design: Test native reusable lesson sequences in {DOCS}, with a bounded helper for drafting a sequence where source text varies. The teacher captures the brief, checks and approves the draft, then conducts and adapts every live activity.
tasks.previous_blocker: Combining reusable activities into a balanced plan takes repeated drafting.
tasks.enabler_now: Activity drafting tools can prepare a proposal from teacher-selected goals and resources.
tasks.still_hard: Making opportunities accessible and adjusting to the actual group.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing when students need more explanation, challenge or independent work.
tasks.altitude: Less sequence drafting; live teaching and learning decisions stay human.

reach.task: Check the balance of instruction and inquiry against learning goals

evidence.claim: Snappet drafts an activity for a lesson goal; this supports draft preparation, not automatic suitability for secondary special education.
The task-specific preparation and delivery shares and savings are E1 estimates.

assumptions: Boundary is activity sequencing and live delivery, excluding separately counted curriculum adaptations and material production. Preparation benefits are assigned once.
The teacher produces goal identifiers, available time, activity resources and minimum access constraints in fully retained s1. No student identity or diagnostic record is sent to the helper.
S2 retains 7.5 hours for correction and unsuitable activity replacement; s3 retains five hours of final review. Missing resources require manual planning.
Test native sequences first; use a model only when adapting the varied activity descriptions. No student assessment or placement decision is automated.
research_questions: Does drafting reduce sequence preparation after checking participation opportunities and accessibility?

already_counted.description: Sequence correction and activity suitability checks

incremental.description: Maintain source activities and drafting instructions

approvals.approved_version: Exact activity sequence, goals, timings, resources and participation constraints; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=10+15*0.50+5+70=92.5; gross=7.5, upkeep=1.5, net=6. High assumes reusable source activities; low assumes corrections leave only 1.5 gross hours offsetting upkeep.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Use audiovisual materials to supplement presentations

steps.what: Select suitable materials and decide accessibility requirements for presentations
Assemble selected media and materials into the presentation
Set up audiovisual equipment and check playback and accessibility
Use computers, audio-visual aids and materials during responsive presentations

tasks.design: Use native reusable layouts and media collections in the {OTHER} presentation software to assemble selected resources. The teacher chooses and checks content, tests actual playback and accessibility, and uses it during the live presentation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated layout and media placement consume preparation time after selection.
tasks.enabler_now: Native templates and reusable packages can reduce that assembly without generating new educational content.
tasks.still_hard: Whether media works for the student's access needs and on actual classroom equipment.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing relevant media and adjusting presentation to student responses.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated assembly; equipment checks and live use remain fully retained.

reach.task: Review whether a presentation format supports the intended learning goal

evidence.claim: Reusable presentation layouts and selected media assembly are E1 proposals; the digest does not establish automatic accessibility assurance.

assumptions: Boundary includes media selection, assembly, setup and use, excluding separate curriculum rewriting and teaching preparation counted elsewhere.

The teacher produces resource identifiers, order, authorised source versions and access requirements in fully retained s1. S2 retains 12.5 hours for assembly checks, captions or alternatives already required by the lesson and manual exceptions.
No automatically correct captions, descriptions or student access flags are assumed. Missing accessible media requires manual replacement and may remove the assembly saving.
Test native layouts and collections first. S3 retains all actual equipment and access testing; no classroom hardware change is proposed.
research_questions: How much assembly time remains after checking links, captions, alternatives and actual playback?

already_counted.description: Media assembly checks and manual accessibility exceptions

incremental.description: Maintain reusable layouts, source permissions and media links

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=20+25*0.50+15+40=87.5; gross=12.5, upkeep=2, net=10.5. High assumes reusable accessible media; low assumes bespoke replacements leave no assembly saving while upkeep remains.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Counselling, inclusive practice judgements and live delivery remain human; requirement retrieval and preparation assembly may shrink.
reach: Clarify inclusive requirements with instructional coordination
Refer specialist concerns to school psychology
role.ambitious_version: Use modest preparation savings for more individual guidance and participation support.
